title: Thicket vs. VetFlow
subject_label: Thicket vs. VetFlow — for Brookside Animal Hospital

sentences.text: Brookside runs three locations in the Hudson Valley with a team of 14, so lead with what happens between the sites rather than with scheduling itself.
Their own appointments page says records requests between locations take one to two business days — that is the problem we remove, and they wrote it down themselves.
They also say online booking is coming soon, which means someone there already owns this decision and has a timeline.
At ten seats, Thicket Multi-Site is $45 per seat per month against VetFlow Clinic at $79 — a difference of $34 per seat per month, or 43%.
Say the comparison carefully: VetFlow Clinic is published as $948 per user per year, so that $79 assumes they commit for twelve months, and VetFlow also holds a five-seat floor where we have none.
VetFlow Enterprise above 25 users is quote-only, so there is no published number to compare against and we should not invent one.
Records sync across locations in real time, with no transfer request and no waiting — Brookside's current one-to-two-day gap is the exact thing this closes.
Full API access is included on Multi-Site at no extra cost, where VetFlow sells the API as a paid add-on and only on Clinic and above.
We are the only scheduling platform built for veterinary practices from the ground up.
We bill monthly with no seat minimum, so a three-location practice can start on the locations that hurt most instead of buying for everyone on day one.
VetFlow integrates with Antech natively and we do not — Antech is on our roadmap for Q1, and if Brookside sends work to Antech that is a real gap today.
Their about page says they use IDEXX in-house at all three locations, so ask before you concede anything; if they are IDEXX-only this gap may not touch them.
VetFlow has an implementation team that gets most practices live in under two weeks, and we do not staff that — be straight about it and offer to run the migration yourself.
They claim over 2,400 practices in North America, which is a fair answer to a reference request and we should not try to match it.
If they mention the VetFlow API — theirs is an add-on on Clinic and above, and the price is quote-only. Ask which systems they need to connect, then tell them ours is included.
If they say VetFlow is cheaper to start — their floor is five users and it is billed annually. Ask how many seats they actually need across the three sites.
If they bring up patient recall — that is their name for automated reminders and we do the same thing. Do not argue the feature; move to what happens between locations.
If they ask about Antech — say no, it is Q1. Then ask what share of their labs go to Antech versus IDEXX, because their own site says IDEXX in-house at all three sites.
If they worry about switching cost — VetFlow's two-week implementation is staffed and ours is not. Offer to do the migration with them and put a date on it.
When a client is seen at Kingston and then comes to Rhinebeck, walk me through what your front desk does today.
Of your 14 people, how many actually need to touch the schedule?
You mention online booking is coming soon — what is driving the timeline on that?
Where do your labs go besides IDEXX in-house?
If you have looked at other systems, what stopped you from moving?
Who else has to say yes to this besides you?

price_comparisons.caveat: VetFlow Clinic is published at $948 per seat per year; normalized to $79.00/seat/month. Assumes a 12-month commitment. VetFlow requires a 5-seat minimum; Thicket has none.
VetFlow Practice is billed annually and requires a 5-seat minimum; Thicket Solo is billed monthly with no minimum. At VetFlow's floor the practice pays for 5 seats whether or not it uses them.
VetFlow Enterprise is quote-only above 25 users. No published price — do not state a comparison.

feature_matrix.why: Brookside runs three locations, so this is table stakes rather than a differentiator.
Brookside's own page admits a one-to-two-day transfer delay; VetFlow's pages do not say either way, so we mark unknown rather than claiming they lack it.
VetFlow calls this patient recall messaging. Same function, different label — not a place to compete.
Included on our Multi-Site tier; a paid add-on for VetFlow on Clinic and above. Nothing on Brookside's site suggests they need it yet.
Brookside runs IDEXX in-house at all three locations, so a gap here would end the conversation.
Our only clear loss on this card. Their lab mix is unknown, which is why it is a discovery question.
A 14-person practice switching systems will ask who does the work. VetFlow claims under two weeks.
Brookside says online booking is coming soon, so they are actively shopping for it.

risk_flags.span: the only scheduling platform built for veterinary practices from the ground up
risk_flags.why: "The only" is an absolute claim with no evidence behind it and is the kind of comparative advertising statement that creates real exposure if the call is recorded or forwarded.
risk_flags.suggested_alternative: built for veterinary practices rather than adapted from human healthcare scheduling

risk_flags.span: VetFlow integrates with Antech natively and we do not
risk_flags.why: This rests on ev_008, fetched 2026-08-02 — more than 30 days old. Integration lists change, and being wrong about a competitor's capability on a live call is worse than hedging.
risk_flags.suggested_alternative: last I checked, VetFlow lists a native Antech integration and we do not yet

risk_flags.span: a difference of $34 per seat per month, or 43%
risk_flags.why: The number is correct but stated without its condition. VetFlow's $79 assumes an annual commitment, and quoting the bare percentage invites a correction on the call.
risk_flags.suggested_alternative: about $34 per seat per month less, though their published rate assumes an annual commitment

risk_flags.span: They claim over 2,400 practices in North America
risk_flags.why: This is VetFlow's own marketing figure with nothing independent behind it. Repeating it as fact lends it credibility we cannot vouch for.

grounding_issues.detail: No evidence_ids. Nothing on any fetched page supports an exclusivity claim about the veterinary scheduling market.
No evidence_ids. Acceptable for a discovery question, which is a prompt rather than a factual claim, but flagged for visibility.
No evidence_ids. Generic qualifying question, not derived from the prospect's page.
Rests on ev_008, fetched 2026-08-02 — 48 days old. Competitor integration pages change without notice.
The 43% figure is arithmetically correct but drops the annual-commitment condition carried in the comparison's caveat.
